title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Chapter III builds 'réseaux' (networks) out of 'découpages'. This is part of Grothendieck's 1980s attempt, announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5, to axiomatise a 'topologie modérée' (tame topology). Here 𝓛 is a one-dimensional object: a 'tranche', essentially a totally ordered set carrying a tameness structure, and 'découpage bien dominé' is a hypothesis on it.

Previous page. It defines:
- closed sub-tranches [a,b], L_{≤a}, L_{≥b} and L itself;
- their boundaries ∂ = {a,b}, {a}, {b}, ∅;
- relative position of two closed sub-tranches, governed by their boundary points;
- open intervals.

This page. The 'tame' finite subsets are controlled by a distinguished family of 2-point subsets, B_0(𝓛) = Dép_2(𝓛). A finite set of points counts as tame ('modérée') when every pair of distinct points in it belongs to Dép_2.

Theorem. Let U ⊂ 𝓛. Suppose there is a finite set I of closed pseudo-découpages (closed sub-tranches) T_i of 𝓛 such that:
(a) for i ≠ j, T_i ∩ T_j = ∅, and T_i, T_j are in 'moderate relative position'. That is, ∂T_i ∪ ∂T_j is a tame finite set: for a ∈ ∂T_i, b ∈ ∂T_j, a ≠ b, the pair {a,b} lies in Dép_2(𝓛).
(b) U = ∪ T_i.
Then:
1. I is unique: the T_i are exactly the connected components of U. Also U = ∅ iff I = ∅.
2. ∂U = ⊔_{i∈I} ∂T_i. Hence ∂U = ∅ iff U = 𝓛 or U = ∅.
Such U are called 'closed moderate parts'.

Definition. Two closed moderate parts X, Y are in moderate relative position if ∂X ∪ ∂Y is tame, i.e. every pair x ∈ ∂X, y ∈ ∂Y with x ≠ y lies in Dép_2.

What it serves. Together with the next page, this sets up the one-dimensional base case of tame topology. The closed tame subsets of a tame line are the finite disjoint unions of closed intervals with tame boundary. The next page closes them under intersection and a 'moderated union' (a supremum in the poset of closed moderate parts), with boundary control (X∩Y)° ⊂ X° ∪ Y°. This is the one-dimensional analogue of 'definable sets in dimension 1 are finite unions of points and intervals' (o-minimality).
errors: The claim that the T_i are the connected components of U, and hence the uniqueness of I, needs that two disjoint closed sub-tranches cannot be 'adjacent'. A discrete order (b immediately followed by b') would break this. Presumably the 'bien dominé' hypothesis, or the condition a ≠ b on boundary points, rules it out, but this is not stated.
'∂U = ∅ iff U = 𝓛 or ∅' implicitly uses connectedness of 𝓛 (it is a single tranche). This is fine but not stated.

The formulation 'for a ∈ ∂T_i, b ∈ ∂T_j, a ≠ b' is ambiguous. It can be read as requiring the boundaries to be disjoint, or as merely excluding coinciding points from the Dép_2 condition. The next page's example [a,b] ∪_mod [b,c] = [a,c] ≠ [a,b] ∪ [b,c] shows that shared boundary points matter, so the convention needs fixing.

ideas.what: Closed 'moderate' subsets of a tame one-dimensional line: finite disjoint unions of closed sub-intervals whose boundary points form a tame finite set. Uniqueness of the decomposition into components, and additivity of boundaries.
ideas.modern_name: Definable closed subsets in dimension 1 of an o-minimal structure (finite unions of intervals and points); cell decomposition in dimension 1
ideas.where_published: Only the programme of 'topologie modérée' is published (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984, §5). The découpage formalism is not.

ideas.what: Tameness of finite point sets defined pairwise, via a distinguished family Dép_2 = B_0 of admissible 2-point subsets ('position relative modérée').
ideas.modern_name: Admissible/tame finite configurations; loosely analogous to 'general position' or definable separation of points

ideas.what: Moderate relative position of two closed moderate parts, defined via their boundaries. This is the hypothesis needed (next page) for the intersection and the 'moderated union' (a supremum) to remain tame.
ideas.modern_name: Transversality/general position of tame subsets; closure of definable families under Boolean operations
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality literature (where closure is axiomatic rather than derived)

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops, in 1986 and independently of o-minimality, an axiomatic tame topology starting from 'découpages'. Here tameness is not closure under Boolean operations, as in o-minimal structures. Instead it is a relative-position condition on boundary points (Dép_2), and Boolean operations are only defined, as 'moderated' operations, for parts in moderate relative position. This programme ('réseaux via découpages') was never published or developed.
missed.quote: ∀ a ∈ ∂T_i, b ∈ ∂T_j, a ≠ b, on a {a,b} ∈ B_0(𝓛) = Dép_2(𝓛) ... (On dit que U est une partie modérée fermée)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a weaker, 'relative' notion of tameness than o-minimality, where unions are replaced by suprema in a poset of tame parts. This could be relevant to combinatorial/PL models of stratified spaces and to the still-open question of what Grothendieck's tame topology was meant to be.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary: one-dimensional interval combinatorics. It matters as a documented fragment of Grothendieck's never-published foundations for 'topologie modérée' via découpages, with an unusual pairwise/relative notion of tameness. That is notable to historians, but the results themselves are routine.
transcription_corrections: 'Psdéf(𝓛)' is likely 'Psdéc(𝓛)' (pseudo-découpages fermés), consistent with the parenthetical 'ens. des ps-découpages fermés'.
The symbol rendered '§T_i' is Grothendieck's boundary notation (∂T_i), matching '∂I' on the previous page. The hatted Û in 2°) is likewise the boundary.
The word before '∀ a ∈ ∂T_i' is more likely 'i.e.'/'à savoir' than 'comme'. Its function is explanatory.
'partie finie modérée formée' is probably 'partie finie modérée' with a struck-out word.
